details: Bitcoin dropped to around $75,000-$76,000, with the broader crypto market shedding tens of billions. This downturn is linked to stalled US-Iran peace talks, which have driven oil prices higher, and investor caution ahead of the Federal Reserve's expected decision to hold interest rates. Persistent inflation and Middle East tensions are reinforcing a cautious monetary outlook, impacting risk assets negatively. Major altcoins have also seen declines.
title: Bitcoin Slides Amid Geopolitical Risks & Central Bank Caution

details: The United Arab Emirates will officially withdraw from OPEC and OPEC+ starting May 1. This move challenges the cartel's unity and has contributed to Brent crude prices surging above $109 a barrel. The development is expected to add to global economic uncertainty and intensify inflation concerns, indirectly impacting risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: UAE Quits OPEC, Raising Oil Market Volatility

details: The European Union has implemented extensive new sanctions aimed at Russia's cryptocurrency sector. These measures seek to disrupt cross-border crypto transactions and limit the liquidity of ruble-based stablecoins, intending to prevent Russia from bypassing traditional financial restrictions. This action highlights the growing intersection of geopolitical conflicts and cryptocurrency regulation.
title: EU Sanctions Target Russian Crypto Industry

details: A White House cryptocurrency advisor has indicated that a major announcement regarding the Trump administration's proposed Strategic Bitcoin Reserve is anticipated in the coming weeks. This potential initiative could significantly influence Bitcoin's market dynamics and further integrate digital currencies into U.S. economic strategy, drawing considerable interest from investors and analysts.
title: White House Advisor Hints at Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
